one_sentence_story: With a clever 1-second black-and-white '2s and 5s' camouflage puzzle in 2001, V. S. Ramachandran and Edward Hubbard proved synesthesia is real sensory perception — driven by cross-activation between neighboring letter-form and V4 color patches on the fusiform gyrus.
so_what_for_you: Notice how naturally even non-synesthetic brains link cross-sensory qualities (sharp sounds to jagged shapes like 'Kiki/Bouba', high pitch to bright colors) — using multi-sensory color and spatial coding makes notes and creative work stickier for everyone.

jargon_map.analogy: an Ishihara color-blindness plate working in reverse.

jargon_map.plain: synesthetes who see color overlaid directly on the printed page vs those experiencing the color vividly inside their mind's eye

jargon_map.plain: universal human tendency (95%+) to match rounded sounds ('Bouba') to soft curves and sharp sounds ('Kiki') to jagged angles
jargon_map.analogy: proof every human brain carries a spark of synesthetic wiring
